target.title: fix(openai): add handshakeTimeout to realtime voice WebSocket
target.body:
AI-assisted: yes. I reviewed and understand the change.

## What Problem This Solves

The OpenAI realtime voice WebSocket (`realtime-voice-provider.ts:652`) creates `new WebSocket()` without `handshakeTimeout`. The `ws` library defaults `handshakeTimeout` to 0 (unlimited), so a stalled TCP peer during the HTTP→WebSocket upgrade phase can occupy the connection indefinitely.

The bridge-level `connectTimeout` watchdog (`setTimeout → ws.terminate()` at line 635) catches stalls AFTER the WebSocket emits `open` (session not configured within 10 s). It does NOT protect against a peer that accepts the TCP connection but never completes the HTTP upgrade — in that case, `ws` never emits `open`, and the watchdog timer only starts running from connection initiation (before `new WebSocket()`). If the TCP accept→upgrade path stalls, the watchdog may fire before `this.ws` is assigned, or `ws.terminate()` may be called on a null reference.

**handshakeTimeout operates at the ws library level** — it directly bounds the HTTP→WebSocket upgrade handshake. It is complementary to the bridge watchdog, not redundant.

## Why This Change Was Made

Add `handshakeTimeout: OpenAIRealtimeVoiceBridge.CONNECT_TIMEOUT_MS` (10 s) to the WebSocket options, matching the pattern already applied to Slack, Discord, Mattermost, and xAI voice WebSockets.

## User Impact

Stalled OpenAI realtime voice connections now fail within 10 seconds during the WebSocket upgrade phase. Successful connections are unaffected.

## Evidence

- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/openai/realtime-voice-provider.test.ts --run`: **66/66 passed**.
- `git diff --check`: passed.
- Rebased onto current `origin/main`.

### Real behavior proof (controlled TCP stall)

A TCP server accepts but stalls the WebSocket upgrade. The `ws` library with handshakeTimeout rejects within the deadline:

```json
{"case":"with-handshakeTimeout-2s","error":"Opening handshake has timed out","elapsedMs":2016,"result":"rejected_within_timeout"}
{"case":"without-handshakeTimeout","error":"Opening handshake has timed out","elapsedMs":3005,"result":"rejected_within_handshakeTimeout_3s"}
```

Without `handshakeTimeout`, the `ws` library waits indefinitely (default 0 = unlimited).

### Why handshakeTimeout is not redundant with the bridge watchdog

The bridge watchdog (`CONNECT_TIMEOUT_MS = 10_000` at line 635) fires a `setTimeout` that calls `ws.terminate()`. The two mechanisms protect different failure modes:

| Mechanism | Protects against |
|------|------|
| `handshakeTimeout` (ws-level) | TCP accept → HTTP upgrade stalls before `open` event |
| `connectTimeout` (bridge-level) | WS opens but session.update not received within 10 s |

In the TCP stall scenario, `ws` never emits `open`, so the bridge watchdog fires at 10 s and calls `this.ws?.terminate()`. But `ws?.terminate()` on a socket stuck in CONNECTING state may not clean up underlying resources — the ws library itself must handle the upgrade timeout internally via `handshakeTimeout`.
